question.text: According to the chapter's historical narrative on the growth of alternative investments, the period described as one of 'unprecedented success for the private equity industry' — during which more money was raised, invested and distributed back to investors than in any other period — is:

answer.text: The 1950s-1960s, when modern portfolio theory emerged
The 1980s boom just before the late-1980s setback
The period since 2014 per the Bain Private Equity Report

explanation.text: The Logic: XIX-D pp. 44-45 cites the Bain Private Equity Report: the period since 2014 was one of unprecedented success for the private equity industry, with more money raised, invested and distributed back to investors than in any other period in the industry's history. The Trap: The 1950s-60s saw modern portfolio theory emerge but not unprecedented PE raising. The 1980s boom ended in setbacks. The dotcom era saw losses, not unprecedented distributions. Note: A 2022-24 slowdown or DPI compression and any LP-pitchbook advice are not in the pages checked, so this explanation rests only on the Bain-cited historical claim.
